card.title: Distance and displacement
card.body: **Distance** ($d$) is the total length of the path traveled — a non-negative scalar. **Displacement** ($\Delta\vec{x} = \vec{x}_f - \vec{x}_i$) is the straight-line vector from the starting position to the final position, so always $|\Delta\vec{x}| \le d$.
card.says: distance counts every step along the path; displacement only cares where you ended up relative to where you started.
card.from: tracking an object's position on a coordinate axis or plane between an initial point and a final point.
card.useWhen: deciding whether direction and backtracking matter — distance adds every segment, while displacement can cancel out or shrink to zero on a round trip.
card.example: Walk $30\text{ m}$ east, then $40\text{ m}$ north. Distance $d = 30 + 40 = 70\text{ m}$. Displacement magnitude $|\Delta\vec{x}| = \sqrt{30^2 + 40^2} = \sqrt{900 + 1600} = 50\text{ m}$ pointing $\approx 53^\circ$ north of east.
card.analogy: Distance is what a car's odometer adds up; displacement is the straight arrow drawn on a map from your starting pin to your ending pin.
